title: Accessibility Plan and Feedback Process

Accessibility Plan and Feedback Process

Executive Summary

Download PDF

Related Links

  • Accessibility Statement
  • Accessibility Plan Progress Report

Saudia is committed to meet the needs of people with disabilities through a vigorous implementation of all disability-related standards and regulations in the countries it operates to. In its home country, Saudi Arabia, the General Authority of Civil Aviation (GACA) has Customer Protection Rights Regulations with strong emphasis on passengers with special needs. In the USA, Saudia has its Air Carrier Access Act (ACAA) Manual that outlines all the measures needed to comply with all regulations related to Nondiscrimination on the Basis of Disability (Part 382).

Likewise, in Canada, Saudia is determined to meet all requirements of the Accessible Canada Act (ACA) and Accessible Transportation for Persons with Disabilities Regulations (ATPDR). Said requirements include:

  • Collecting and compiling feedback from guests and our own employees on how to better service passengers with disability; and
  • Maintaining and updating its Accessibility Plan and reporting requirements.

This plan summarizes our commitment to improving passenger accessibility by identifying and removing all accessibility barriers and coming up with policies and procedures that advance this objective.

General

This Accessibility Plan represents Saudia’s firm commitment in maintaining a convenient, positive and barrier-free guest experience. Furthermore, we will continue to improve all forms of accessibility in all of the airline’s guest touch points, which will be reflected in our service policies and procedures.

As part of its commitment to its implementation, Saudia has designated a senior-level manager to accept, review and act on feedback:

Manager – Policies, Governance & Compliance
Saudia
Head Office, Khaledia District
PO Box 620, Loc 130
Jeddah, Saudi Arabia 21235

Feedback

The manager receiving accessibility feedback is a member of our larger DOT/CTA Task Force organized to handle all disability and accessibility-related issues, including soliciting and receiving feedback from various sources on behalf of Saudia.

Feedback collection

All feedback, anonymous or not, comments and suggestions on our Accessibility Plan are welcome. Feedback with the exception of anonymous feedback will be acknowledged in the same manner it was received. Such feedback or requests for a copy of our Accessibility Plan in various alternate formats may be sent through:

Email: accessibility@saudia.com

Snail Mail:
Saudia Accessibility Plan Feedback
Attention: DOT/CTA Task Force
8081 Wolftrap Road, Suite 200
Vienna, VA, USA 22148

Phone: Toll Free: 1-855-588-0999

Online form:
For added convenience, an online feedback form has been made available by Saudia for submission of comments and suggestions regarding accessibility at: Complaints And Feedback (saudia.com).

Such feedback will be used to determine accessibility issues and prioritize the most important ones.
Anonymous submissions will be allowed.

Feedback response

All feedback will be accepted and reviewed but only those with contact information will be acknowledged by Saudia. Such feedback will be managed according to Saudia policies and procedures, including its Privacy Policy.

Information and Communication Technologies (ICT)

Saudia is committed to using all forms of digital technology and innovation to ensure its on-line services, including website, applications and digital content, are accessible to people with disabilities including those who use screen reader technology. All measures are being undertaken to achieve this.

Saudia believes in continuous improvement of its technology, particularly as it relates to accessibility. Such improvements are always on-going and will be continuous since technology is always subject to changes and innovation.

Saudia’s website is managed using the latest Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.0 Level AA Success Criteria to make it accessible to a worldwide audience, including end-users with disability. We strive to deliver the best website experience to users by constantly improving and upgrading the system, irrespective of technology or physical barriers.

Saudia’s web accessibility compliance is further covered in its Accessibility Statement: Accessibility.

An internal Task Force, which will assess and evaluate Saudia’s on-going accessibility initiatives has been organized.

Also, part of the initiatives is to ensure in-terminal announcements are in both audio and visual formats, which is already being practices in all Saudia gateways in the USA and Canada.

Meantime, the possibility of engaging third-party accessibility audit resources is being studied.

Communication other than ICT

Communication – in all its forms, is central to Saudia’s guest service and is always at or near the top of its priority list. Its Accessibility Plan therefore recognizes the importance of building in communication in every facet of its accessibility initiatives. This includes communication regarding the introduction of new services, new routes, changes and upgrades to existing products and others.

Saudia may rely on third-party service providers if there is a need for updates or changes under the ATPDR. In addition, Saudia has integrated systems that provide information at different guest touchpoints, available in audio, visual and other alternative formats. These systems are being reviewed, updated and upgraded to comply with ATPDR.

  • Teletypewriter/test display device (TTY) – Saudia is making arrangements to provide TTY access service, with a target date for completion in June 2026.
  • In-person interaction – Our ground agents and cabin crew undergo sensitivity training, among other things, to ensure they always communicate with our guests, especially those with disabilities, to see if they need assistance.
  • Aircraft – Saudia is taking steps to equip its aircraft with English and Arabic braille passenger safety feature cards as well as large print, and braille formats of the Air Passenger Protection Regulation (APPR), which are available upon request. Completion date is set for June 2026. Individual briefings are also to be provided for important information such as the location of call buttons.

Procurement of goods, services, and facilities

Saudia supports the Accessible Canada Act (ACA) by ensuring that the procurement of goods and services for Saudia’s operations in Canada include accessibility as one of its key factors in the selection of vendors and service providers. This results in identifying potential accessibility barriers and fixing the issues while preventing new ones from taking place.

Saudia complies with all regulatory requirements of every country it operates in. Accessibility standards are, whenever possible, built into procurement processes and accessibility criteria considered when purchasing new goods and services, to make sure deliverables have accessibility features:

  • Procedures are in place to make sure accessibility standards are applied to the procurement of products and services. These are intended to bring the products or services aligned with standards in place, or if otherwise, proper mitigation steps will be taken or developed.
  • If goods and services needed cannot comply with or meet ATPDR accessibility standards, the procedures will require that clear justifications will be provided and documented.
  • Should a supplier fail to meet the accessibility standards required by procedures, Saudia will determine if the supplier offers goods or services that are flexible and have built-in features or functions to provide accessibility to the greatest number of users.

Saudia will study the possibility of using focus groups to test accessibility features for new services before implementation.

In the future, Saudia will do its best to build-in accessibility features in the early stages of product development, including business case submissions and evaluation, justification requirements for items that fall short of accessibility standards, project management and other business processes. These may include Service Level Agreements (SLAs), Request for Proposals (RFPs) and others.

  • These processes and documents form Saudia’s body of work supporting accessibility standards including suitability of new aircraft purchases, compliance of the website, mobile app and other digital media with WCAG standards and others.

Design and delivery of programs and services

It is Saudia’s commitment to improve accessibility and usability of its key Sales and Communication channels, including on our website. Saudia tries to constantly ensure that website services, applications, and content are accessible to guests with disabilities including users of screen reader technology.

Saudia complies with (WCAG).2.0 AA and meet the Canadian Transportation Agency’s Accessible Transportation for Persons with Disabilities Regulations, as well as the U.S. Department of Transportation Ruling under 14 CFR Part 382, Nondiscrimination on the Basis of Disability in Air Travel. Furthermore, we are working towards WCAG 2.1 AA conformance to meet the Canadian and U.S requirements and the requirements of the European Union Web Accessibility Directive.

To do this, Saudia has shortlisted a number of web accessibility consultants to help test, develop, remediate, and maintain our website in-line with the latest Web Content Accessibility Guidelines.

Our guests are advised to self-identify their accessibility needs through all our guest touchpoints, from flight reservations to arrival so that our trained staff can assist them as needed at any point of their journey.

Saudia is working towards full compliance with the Accessible Transportation for Persons with Disabilities Regulations Parts 1 and 2 of this regulation for all flights operated to and from Canada.

Saudia’s flights to and from the United States also follows the Passenger with Disabilities Passenger Bill of Rights under the U.S. Air Carrier Access Act and its implementing regulation, 14 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) Part 382.

Saudia’s flights to and from the United States also follow the Passenger with Disabilities Passenger Bill of Rights under the U.S. Air Carrier Access Act and its implementing regulation, 14 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) Part 382.

Initial training will be delivered to frontline Saudia personnel, with recurrent training every three years to ensure all content, accessibility guidelines, policies, procedures and standards are updated and complied with.

Transportation

Saudia complies with accessibility regulations of countries it operates in, to include the Accessible Transportation for Persons with Disabilities Regulations, in which Saudia is considered a large carrier required to comply with Parts 1 and 2 of this regulation. Furthermore, Saudia is compliant with the U.S. Department of Transportation 14 CFR Part 382.

Saudia commits to:

  • Provide frontline employees with sensitivity training to identify, assist and support persons with disability.
  • Provide accessibility assistance for guests who self-identity as having disability during the booking process, on the ground at the airport and in the air while on board the aircraft.
  • Provide regular check-in procedures for guests with disability.

The Built Environment

  • Airport lounges – Saudia’s airport lounges – whether its own in its home base in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, or the airport lounges it contracts with in the airports it operates to in Canada, USA and other cities worldwide, are compliant with accessibility standards, providing open seating, and accessible lavatories.
  • Aircraft fleet – Saudia’s aircraft have on-board wheelchairs and wheelchairs accessible lavatories on selected aircraft. Certain aircraft types have passenger seats with moveable armrests, which are placed throughout the aircraft.

Saudia is open to all comments and feedback received from our guests regarding accessibility for our different guest touchpoints on the ground and in the air, including ground facilities and aircraft features, as well as our workplaces for employees.

Provisions of CTA accessibility-related regulations

As a large carrier under Canadian Transportation Agency regulations, Saudia has to comply with all provisions of the Accessible Transportation for Persons with Disabilities Regulations (SOR/2019-244) contained in parts 1 and 2 applicable to foreign carriers.

Consultations

To help in the preparation of its Accessibility Plan, Saudia formed a Task Force composed of managers and staff with wide ranging expertise.

It has communicated with disability advocacy groups as well as individuals with disability, including employees who may have or have family members who themselves have disabilities. This ensures constant feedback and interaction with relevant groups and organizations.

Saudia commits itself to developing employee and guest service policies that comply with Accessible Transportation for Persons with Disabilities Regulations (ATPDR).

Our policies and procedures related to accessibility will be developed in consultation with persons with disabilities.

External consultations

Saudia is in discussions with Open Doors Organization, a US 501(c) 3 public charity non-profit with a mission to make goods and services accessible to people with disabilities in travel, tourism and transportation. Such discussions include consultations to review and develop its training programs for sensitivity and proper handling and communication with passengers with disabilities. Focus groups with passengers with disability are part of the plan. A comprehensive review of the training will be conducted, and relevant feedback built into the programs.

Saudia’s commitment to continuous consultations covers all types of accessibility challenges, including:

  • Website and mobile app accessibility.
  • Training requirements for frontline staff to provide disability assistance.
  • Facilitating provision of medical assistance in-flight.
  • Ensuring adequate staffing during peak seasons to provide accessibility services.

Internal consultations

Saudia will undertake efforts to consult employees who either have friends and relatives who have disabilities or are themselves disabled. Saudia employees will be asked to share their ideas, comments and suggestions on workplace accessibility to determine any barriers to accessibility from hiring to on-boarding and orientation to regular work.

Saudia further commits to regular company communication, as part of its Transformation Program, to invite insights and input on various regarding accessibility with relevant discussions to be featured on the e-staff and transformation portals.

Meantime, Saudia will continue to identify and provide solutions to accessibility challenges, including:

  • Reviewing and revising policies and procedures to remove obstacles to accessibility in coordination with managers, supervisors and employees.
  • Determining employee accessibility requirements throughout their employment.
  • Providing the latest technology and assistive devices in anticipation of accessibility needs when they arise.

Saudia Americas Region has created an Accessibility Task Force charged with implementing all related rules and regulations that address accessibility and disability issues. These include Canada’s ATPDR and USA’s ACAA, Part 382 Nondiscrimination Against Disability. The task force will meet regularly and provide self-audit reports, minutes of meetings and action items. Obstacles, barriers and other recurring issues will be thoroughly discussed with the end of view of resolving such issues.
